title: NHC blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into official Hurricane Melissa forecasts before its Category 5 landfall in Jamaica
summary: The US National Hurricane Center blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into its Melissa forecasts from 21 October 2025; the center's track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean.
account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. NHC's guidance labels the model's ensemble mean GDMI. Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. Discussion 8, on 23 October, moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. It set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, Discussion 13 noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. Discussion 14 put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. NHC's own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its Melissa track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. NHC's 2025 verification report, dated 30 March 2026, says that its track errors were notably lower than average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.
purpose: Google DeepMind's experimental model gives National Hurricane Center forecasters ensemble guidance on the track and intensity of tropical cyclones.
system: Google DeepMind AI hurricane forecast model, ensemble mean designated GDMI in NHC guidance
taxonomy_note: The AI model's contribution to official forecasts is read as forecast accuracy, with no error figure for this storm.

ratings.reason: No cited source attributes an outcome for any individual to the AI guidance. The sources report impacts only for the population as a whole.

NHC forecasters blended the DeepMind ensemble into official track forecasts from Discussion 1 and set intensity forecasts closest to it from Discussion 10. Melissa's official track error at 120 hours was 87.7 nautical miles, against a five-year mean of 185.4 nautical miles. NHC's Science Operations Officer called the AI guidance very valuable for Melissa.

No source reports that the AI guidance changed preparations or losses in Jamaica. The forecasts covered a Category 5 landfall that affected about 1.6 million people, and the IFRC approved its emergency allocation five days ahead.

ai_role.statement: NHC forecasters state in Discussions 1, 2, 8, 10, 12, 13 and 14 that they blended official track and intensity forecasts with Google DeepMind's ensemble or aligned them with it. CNN reports that NHC forecasters credit the model with early confidence in rapid intensification, and Lowry judges that it gave forecasters confidence for aggressive forecasts. The official forecast remains a human synthesis of several aids, and no source isolates the AI's effect on outcomes in Jamaica.

fields.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. NHC's guidance labels the model's ensemble mean GDMI. Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. Discussion 8, on 23 October, moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. It set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, Discussion 13 noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. Discussion 14 put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. NHC's own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its Melissa track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. NHC's 2025 verification report, dated 30 March 2026, says that its track errors were notably lower than average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.

NHC forecasters blended the DeepMind ensemble into official track forecasts from Discussion 1 and set intensity forecasts closest to it from Discussion 10. Melissa's official track error at 120 hours was 87.7 nautical miles, against a five-year mean of 185.4 nautical miles. NHC's Science Operations Officer called the AI guidance very valuable for Melissa.

No source reports that the AI guidance changed preparations or losses in Jamaica. The forecasts covered a Category 5 landfall that affected about 1.6 million people, and the IFRC approved its emergency allocation five days ahead.

display.answer: Ten of the twelve cited sources come from the deployer's side: six NHC forecast discussions, a landfall update, the 2025 verification report, the Melissa tropical cyclone report and a National Weather Service interview with NHC's Science Operations Officer. Both independent sources, CNN and Michael Lowry's newsletter, draw on retired NHC forecaster James Franklin. CNN also interviewed NHC staff. The figures on deaths and damage come from IFRC reports, which do not isolate the AI's effects.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: The US National Hurricane Center blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into its Melissa forecasts from 21 October 2025; the center's track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean.
fields.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. NHC's guidance labels the model's ensemble mean GDMI. Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. Discussion 8, on 23 October, moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. It set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, Discussion 13 noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. Discussion 14 put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. NHC's own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its Melissa track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. NHC's 2025 verification report, dated 30 March 2026, says that its track errors were notably lower than average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.
